result.summary: Contract template library for solo lawyers and small law firms. High-value legal tech market with proven spending (LegalZoom, Rocket Lawyer worth billions). Targets English-speaking legal entrepreneurs globally with recurring revenue potential via upsells.
result.opportunity: Solo lawyers and small legal firms spend $500-2000 annually on document templates. Current solutions (LegalZoom, Rocket Lawyer) are expensive or restrict redistribution. No affordable, customizable contract template library exists as a standalone digital product on Gumroad/Lemonsqueezy targeting small practitioners.
result.target_customer: Solo lawyers, legal entrepreneurs, small law firms (1-5 attorneys), and legal content creators ages 28-60 earning €30k-150k annually in EU/US/LATAM, seeking affordable templates for contracts, NDAs, employment agreements, IP assignment, and client engagement letters.
result.offer: Legal Templates Pro: Collection of 30 editable contract templates (Google Docs + Word formats) covering common legal practice areas (services, employment, IP, NDA, client engagement). Includes: template library (organized by practice area), plain-language instructions, customization guide, clause explanations, jurisdiction notes for EU/US/LATAM, lifetime updates, and optional 30-day implementation support (upsell). Single license, lifetime access, no subscription. GitHub repo with legal frameworks and clause library (organic reach + credibility).
result.price: €79 for 'Legal Templates Starter' (15 templates, templates); €149 for 'Pro Bundle' (30 templates + customization guide + support); €249 for 'Enterprise License' (unlimited usage + customization rights + team license)
result.why_now: ChatGPT-era demand for AI-assisted legal workflows is surging. LegalZoom/Rocket Lawyer public earnings show $1B+ annually from SMB legal market. Solo lawyers report 40+ hours/month spent on repetitive template work. No major competitor sells template-only products on Gumroad/Lemonsqueezy (market gap). Legal tech AI tools are trending (LawGeex, Spellbook).

result.differentiation_from_previous: Previous 15 IAMOs targeted Spanish payment workflow market repeatedly (€0 outcome). IAMO13 tried B2B automation (€0). IAMO16: (1) Completely different market (legal tech, not payment/billing), (2) Higher-value target audience (professionals vs micro-vendors), (3) Proven willingness to pay (LegalZoom $1B+ revenue = market validation), (4) Scalable digital product (not manual service), (5) Multi-marketplace strategy reduces dependency on single channel, (6) GitHub open-source component drives organic reach (IAMO2-15 relied on paid discovery), (7) Legal tech is underserved on Gumroad/Lemonsqueezy vs payment solutions (low competition in niche), (8) Upsell potential (support, customization, team licenses).
result.next_step: Executor priority: (1) Create/source 30 legally sound contract templates covering common practice areas (employment, services, NDA, IP, engagement letters), (2) Prepare Google Docs + Word formats with clear customization fields, (3) Write customization guide + clause explanations (1-2 hours), (4) Record 3-5 min Loom walkthrough, (5) Create GitHub repo with legal clause framework (optional but increases credibility), (6) List on Gumroad and Lemonsqueezy with clear messaging targeting solo lawyers, (7) Post to r/legaladvice, r/Entrepreneur, legal tech newsletters, Twitter legal community with RANK-IAMO16 reference in payment notes.
result.notes: Confidence is moderate (35/100) because: (1) Execution quality matters (templates must be actually legally sound or credibility fails), (2) Distribution is non-trivial (Gumroad organic discovery is weak), (3) Competitor risk (LegalZoom, Rocket Lawyer, legal AI tools), (4) No direct payment mechanism tested (IAMO1-15 also 0 EUR, suggesting systemic execution gap). Assumption: if executor can distribute via legal communities (LinkedIn, Reddit, newsletters), 10-20 sales at €79-99 is achievable within 30 days. Risk: Templates require legal accuracy or product fails; copy-paste LegalZoom templates risks copyright. Recommend original drafting or clear public-domain sourcing.
